payload.name: hol-rulebook
payload.problem_domain: Heroes of Legend TTRPG rulebook chapter review and disposition

payload.statement:
Chapter under review: ch19 (quarto-book/chapters/19-gm-guidance.qmd), "Dungeon Architect's Guide", 566 lines.

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files a finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope
Findings cite [file:line] in the chapter (19-gm-guidance.qmd). Mechanics
findings state the broken value and the expected value. Cross-chapter checks
use the authoritative chapters as the reference, not this chapter (core
rules = ch06: success tiers, difficulty ladder +2 Easy / +0 Standard / -2
Hard / -4 Very Hard, Boon/Bane; combat = ch13: conditions incl. Prone,
one-roll principle, modifiers, W/S/S damage; disciplines/economy = ch08: DP,
ladder, progression; classes = ch05: the nine classes and their names;
attributes = ch03: the -2 to +2 ceiling; skills = ch07: the 23-skill roster
and costs, Skill (Attribute) check format; advancement = ch18: leveling,
milestones, strongholds @sec-strongholds (base 50 HP, Fortify action),
faction reputation ladder; magic items = ch17: named unique cards, rarity
ladder, no flat-bonus generics; bestiary = ch20: stat block format and the
monster challenge bands; spell chains = ch11/ch12: card format and specific
cantrips; glossary = ch21; reference tables = ch22).

Disposition classes (for the librarian's synthesis):
  mechanical    - safe to implement as a micro-PR (headings, tables, wording,
                  em-dashes, single-cell refs, budget rows, worked-example
                  arithmetic that is canon-determined by another chapter)
  substantive   - needs a dispatched implementation pass (multi-file, new
                  content, worked-example rewrite requiring new narrative)
  design-decision - needs Bruce's ruling; implement the recommended default,
                  flagged veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md

Standing book conventions are in force: zero em-dashes in book text; damage
and healing budgets flat at Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21;
monster stat blocks conform to challenge bands (C1-2 -> 2/4/6, C3-6 ->
6/9/12, C7+ -> 9/15/21; secondary attacks at most one tier lower than the
primary; monster HP is a guideline, never a deviation); card costs 2/4/8 DP;
Adept prereqs exactly 2, Master exactly 3; no flat +N damage riders anywhere
in the book (a damage bonus must be a budget row, a Basic-card floor of
1/2/3 + attribute, or a "+1 damage tier" bump); no flat "+N to a check"
riders where the book convention is Boon/Bane; one-roll principle (the hit
or casting roll IS the outcome, no second damage roll); damage dice are dead
outside the allowed random-table exceptions (1d4/1d6 random behavior, 1d4+1
duration dice); attribute ceiling -2 to +2; class names are exactly the nine
from ch05 (Protector, Blade, Arcanist, Shepherd, Intellect, Odd, Leader,
Unbalanced, Shadow - "cleric", "wizard", "fighter", "warlock" as class nouns
are stale vocabulary); level-gated conditions use the leveled vocabulary
(Burning X, Frozen X, Poisoned X, Slowed X, Dazed X - no bespoke phrasing);
checks are written as Skill (Attribute) or plain skill names, never mixed
skill-and-attribute lists. Violations of these conventions are findings, not
questions.

Scope note: this chapter is the canonical home for DA guidance, encounter
building, treasure pacing, resting, exploration, crafting, resource
management, corruption, the faction system (@sec-faction-system), the
sample adventure "The Sunken Vault", and the card templates
(@sec-card-templates). Where another chapter contradicts it, the finding
should name BOTH files and identify which is canonical. The council's
output is a disposition plan; it does not itself edit the book.

payload.argument: The chapter fails several load-bearing mechanics conventions, so it cannot ship as written. Kelvath (19-gm-guidance.qmd:304) is Challenge 2 yet his two primaries deal 6/9/12, a whole band above the 2/4/6 his rating requires (ch20's Challenge 2 Bear hits at 2/4/6), and his seal-break line grants a flat +1 damage bonus where the book only allows tier-bump language. The spell-card template example (lines 512-514) teaches flat +2/+3 center-target riders that exist on no budget row; the same illegal riders appear in the ch11 published card, so the fix spans both files. The faction actions Train (line 438) and Fortify Position (line 440) grant +1 to a skill and +5 temporary HP, but ch18's canonical Train and Fortify grant +2 and +10 and explicitly reference these faction actions, so the values must reconcile to +2 and +10. Treasure pacing (line 69) cites a generic +1 sword, which ch17 bans outright. The adventure hooks (line 345) and treasure talk (line 71) use warlock, cleric, and fighter as class nouns, none of which are among ch05's nine classes (expected Unbalanced, Shepherd, Blade). A one-use poultice (line 227) heals 3 HP and a narrated Standard hit (line 289) deals 3 damage; both numbers are off the Novice 2/4/6 budget, expected 4 for the Standard hit and a 2-or-4 heal. Check shapes drift from Skill (Attribute): line 159 inverts to Fortitude (Endurance) and lines 214 and 312 offer skill-or-attribute either/or lists. Minor items: 1d3 delivery time (line 461) is outside the allowed dice set, and the template's '3+ = Master' (line 501) should read exactly 3. Most fixes are single-value mechanical edits; the template example and Kelvath also need alignment with ch11 and ch20.

evidence.claim: The Kelvath stat block lists both primary attacks at 6/9/12 despite a Challenge 2 rating, one full band above the 2/4/6 row that tier requires per ch20's challenge bands (the Challenge 2 Bear in ch20 deals 2/4/6), and the seal-break clause adds a flat +1 damage bonus instead of a damage-tier bump.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Warden's Blade: 6/9/12 slashing. Water Bolt: 6/9/12

evidence.claim: The spell template's Brimstone Burst example has budget-correct Adept damage (6/9/12) but bolts flat +2 and +3 bonuses onto center targets that match no budget row; the published ch11 card carries the same riders and its Burning keyword is swapped for Area in the template copy.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: targets at the center take +2.

evidence.claim: The Fortify Position faction action promises +5 temporary HP to a stronghold, while ch18's Fortify action grants +10 temporary HP and states it stacks with this very faction action, so the two values must agree at +10.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: the stronghold gains +5 temporary HP.

evidence.claim: The faction Train action hands out +1 to one skill for a session, but ch18's Train gives +2 to one skill and says it replaces the Train faction action, so ch19's +1 contradicts the canonical +2.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Gain a +1 bonus to one skill

evidence.claim: Treasure pacing suggests a generic +1 sword as a level-2 milestone prize, directly contradicting ch17's rule that every magic item is a named unique card and no generic +1 sword exists; the example should name a unique weapon.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: A +1 sword at level 2 is a big deal.

evidence.claim: The adventure's continuation hooks describe the warlock's pendant, the cleric's holy symbol, and the fighter's family crest, three class nouns absent from ch05's nine classes (expected Unbalanced, Shepherd, and Blade), and the treasure section repeats 'fighter' when discussing armor upgrades.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: the party's warlock's pendant. Or the cleric's holy symbol.

evidence.claim: Two printed numbers sit off the healing/damage budget: a one-use poultice restores 3 HP and a narrated Standard hit lands 3 damage, while the Novice budget rows are 2/4/6, so the heal should be 2 or 4 and the Standard hit 4.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: a healing poultice (heals 3 HP, one use)

evidence.claim: Check shapes drift from the Skill (Attribute) convention: one roll is written attribute-first as Fortitude (Endurance), and two rolls offer skill-or-attribute either/or lists (Knowledge or Persuasion; Arcana or Reason), which the check-format rule forbids.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: an Arcana or Reason check (Hard, -2)

payload.argument: The chapter does not hold up under arithmetic and convention auditing and cannot ship as written. The adventure boss at 19-gm-guidance.qmd:304 sits at Challenge 2 yet both of its attack lines read 6/9/12, the Adept row, while the bestiary's monster creation bands (ch20:304-307) cap challenges 1-2 at 2/4/6; the fix is to drop both attack rows to 2/4/6 or raise the Challenge into the C3-6 band. The same stat block's Seal-Bound adds a flat +1 to all damage, which the book's damage-rider convention forbids; the permitted form is a one-tier bump, exactly the phrasing this chapter applies to Water Bolt at line 314. The narrated first combat at line 289 shows a Weak hit for 2 and a Standard hit for 3 against a guardian whose block lists DR 1 and the 2/4/6 row, so the pair cannot both be right under a single DR reading (DR applied gives 1 and 3, no DR gives 2 and 4). The group skill challenge at lines 235 and 253-257 stops counting at two failures yet lists a three-plus-failures outcome that is unreachable under that stopping rule, and the tier table's Weak row is itself a qualified success, so no rolled result actually constitutes a failure. The rations rule at line 159 writes the check as Fortitude (Endurance), but Endurance is the skill and Fortitude the attribute per ch07:110, so the parenthetical is reversed. The Fortify Position faction action at line 440 grants +5 temporary HP while ch18:137's Fortify stronghold action grants +10 for the same purpose and states the two stack, so the values should be harmonized. Hooks prose at line 345 and treasure advice at line 71 use warlock, cleric, and fighter, none of which appear among the nine classes in ch05:8, and line 69 paces a generic +1 sword that ch17:13 declares never appears; flat +N check riders at lines 251, 334, 438, and 143-145 conflict with the Boon/Bane convention ch17 items follow. On the support side, every @sec- cross-reference resolves (ch08:172, ch13:1, ch14:1, plus in-chapter anchors), the card templates at lines 489-558 match ch05/ch08/ch11 canon, and monster conventions such as Undead Nature, Vulnerable, Recharge, and Morale align with ch20. Most repairs are mechanical value swaps, but the skill-challenge outcome table and the adventure's narrated damage values need substantive rewrites.

evidence.claim: Kelvath's blade and bolt both use the Adept-tier damage row 6/9/12 although Challenge 2 belongs to the C1-2 band, which the bestiary creation rules cap at 2/4/6; broken 6/9/12, expected 2/4/6 (or a Challenge of 3+).
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Warden's Blade: 6/9/12 slashing. Water Bolt: 6/9/12

evidence.claim: Seal-Bound grants a flat +1 to all damage once the seal breaks, violating the book rule that damage boosts must be a budget row, a basic-card floor, or a one-tier bump; broken flat +1, expected the +1 damage tier phrasing the chapter itself uses for Water Bolt at line 314.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: gains +1 to all damage

evidence.claim: The narrated first-combat hits deal 2 on Weak and 3 on Standard against a Drowned Guardian carrying DR 1 and the 2/4/6 row, so the numbers are mutually inconsistent: applying DR yields 1 and 3, ignoring it yields 2 and 4; broken pair (2, 3), expected (1, 3) or (2, 4).
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Standard, 3 damage. Water pours from the wound.

evidence.claim: The group challenge stops at two failures yet its outcome table lists a three-plus-failures row that can never occur under that cap, and the per-check tier table treats Weak as a success at a cost, so the threshold's failure condition has no defined trigger; broken unreachable 3+ row, expected a defined failure result and a reachable outcome space.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 3+ failures (exhausted all attempts)

evidence.claim: The rations rule calls for a Fortitude (Endurance) roll, but the skills chapter keys the Endurance skill to the Fortitude attribute, so the skill and attribute are swapped; broken Fortitude (Endurance), expected Endurance (Fortitude).
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: make a Fortitude (Endurance) roll each day

evidence.claim: The Fortify Position faction action grants +5 temporary HP while the advancement chapter's Fortify stronghold action grants +10 for the same defensive effect and notes the two actions stack; broken +5, expected +10 to match ch18:137.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: the stronghold gains +5 temporary HP

evidence.claim: A continuing-hooks line names a warlock's pendant, a cleric's holy symbol, and a fighter's family crest, but none of warlock, cleric, or fighter is among the nine class names in ch05:8, which the book treats as stale vocabulary; broken stale class nouns, expected Shadow, Shepherd, and Blade equivalents.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: the party's warlock's pendant. Or the cleric's holy symbol

evidence.claim: Flat numeric check bonuses appear in the Circlet of the Warden (+2, line 334), the skill challenge's Strong-result +2 (line 251), the Train faction action +1 (line 438), and the crafting +1/-1 outcomes (lines 143-145), while ch17 expresses such effects as Boon/Bane and bans flat +N check riders; broken flat +N, expected Boon/Bane phrasing.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: grants +2 to a check against being moved

payload.argument: The chapter cannot ship as-is: it contains at least five mechanics breaks plus convention violations. [304] Kelvath is rated Challenge 2 but deals 6/9/12, the damage row every C3-6 monster uses; the C2 Ogre and Dire Boar in the bestiary both deal 2/4/6, so either his rating or his damage is wrong, and his seal-break 'gains +1 to all damage' is a flat rider the book bans in favor of damage-tier bumps. [513-514] The chapter's own Brimstone Burst example adds flat +2/+3 damage at the center, teaching the exact off-budget rider the damage table forbids. [235,257] The approach challenge ends at 2 failures yet lists a 3-failures outcome that can never trigger, and a three-player party making one check each cannot mathematically reach 3 successes, leaving the 2-successes-1-failure exhaustion case with no defined resolution. [53] The encounter multiplier never says what a budget point buys or how party size scales it, so a six-player table and a three-player table get the same fight. [69] Treasure pacing hands the party 1-2 items per level and endorses a generic +1 sword, contradicting ch17's per-hero Uncommon cadence and its explicit ban on generic +1 swords. [437,392] Every player can take Spread Influence in the same downtime for a party-wide reputation bump whose +2 cap is ambiguous, while the betrayal penalty reads as both subtract-three and set-to-Hostile. [310] The tactical note claims Water Bolt outranges bows, but bestiary bows reach 80 ft and the 20-ft tether around a central pedestal covers the whole 40-ft chamber, so an archer can stand in the corridor outside his 30-ft reach and shoot him freely. [345,257,159,461] Adventure text uses stale class nouns (warlock/cleric/fighter), a surprise round ch13 explicitly disallows, a reversed Fortitude (Endurance) check format, and a 1d3 roll outside the allowed dice.

evidence.claim: Kelvath's stat block breaks the locked challenge bands: rated Challenge 2 yet using the 6/9/12 row reserved for C3-6 monsters, plus a seal-break bonus written as a flat +1 damage rider instead of a tier bump.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Warden's Blade: 6/9/12 slashing

evidence.claim: The Brimstone Burst example card adds flat damage to center targets, an off-budget rider the damage conventions reserve for tier bumps.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: targets at the center take +2

evidence.claim: The approach challenge terminates at two failures yet lists a three-plus-failures outcome, and parties of three or fewer cannot reach three successes with one check per character, leaving exhaustion undefined.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The party needs 3 successes before 2 failures

evidence.claim: The x1-to-x4 encounter multiplier never defines what a budget point buys or how party size scales it, so a six-player table builds the same fight as a three-player table.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Encounter difficulty uses a simple multiplier against party level

evidence.claim: Treasure guidance contradicts the item chapter: it paces one to two items per level for the whole party and endorses a generic +1 sword, while ch17 grants an Uncommon per hero by level 3 and bans generic +1 swords.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: A +1 sword at level 2 is a big deal

evidence.claim: The reputation economy is gameable: every player may take Spread Influence in the same downtime for a party-wide bump whose +2 cap is ambiguous, and the betrayal penalty reads as both subtract-three and set-to-Hostile.

evidence.claim: The boss's tether is geometrically meaningless in a forty-foot chamber and the tactical note overstates Water Bolt's reach against bestiary bows, so an archer retreating down the corridor can shoot Kelvath from beyond his 30-foot range.

evidence.claim: Adventure text uses stale class nouns for the pendant hook, a surprise round mechanic ch13 explicitly disallows, a reversed attribute-skill check format for starvation, and a 1d3 delivery roll outside the allowed dice.

payload.argument: The chapter's voice holds up: the first-person Dungeon Architect narrator, the direct-address read-aloud passages, and the informal asides all match the register established in the introduction chapter, so the sample adventure reads like part of the same book. What breaks publishability is vocabulary and format discipline, not tone. Party references use stale class labels at [19-gm-guidance:345] (warlock/cleric/fighter) and [19-gm-guidance:71] (the fighter), though ch05 defines nine classes and none is named that. Check calls drift: [19-gm-guidance:159] reverses the chapter's own Skill (Attribute) order, and [19-gm-guidance:312] merges a skill and an attribute into one either/or roll. The art captions at [19-gm-guidance:7] and [19-gm-guidance:9] are the chapter's only 'GM' usages where the book says DA. Faction perks labeled 'boon' ([19-gm-guidance:420], [19-gm-guidance:461]) collide with the Boon mechanic keyword in the core rules. The reputation ladder is duplicated between the table at [19-gm-guidance:368] and the benefits list at [19-gm-guidance:401], and the card section alternates spelled-out tiers at [19-gm-guidance:510] with W/S/St shorthand at [19-gm-guidance:540]. Each fix is a small, local edit: rename the class references, normalize check phrasing, retitle the faction perk, merge or cross-reference the ladder copies, and pick one tier-abbreviation style. No structural rewrite is required.

evidence.claim: The continuing-hooks list suggests matching a keepsake to 'the party's warlock', 'the cleric', or 'the fighter', three labels that are not among the book's nine class names, so the passage reads like leftover vocabulary from an older draft.

payload.argument: The chapter is not publishable as-is on the editorial lens; four defect families block it. First, the approach skill challenge contradicts itself: the text ends the group attempt at two failures [19-gm-guidance.qmd:235] while the outcomes table lists a third row keyed to three-plus failures that can never occur once the challenge has already stopped at two [19-gm-guidance.qmd:257]; the threshold sentence and the table must be reconciled. Second, the card-template section misstates the book's card grammar: the declared spell label '(Spell)' appears on no published card (the book uses Cantrip, Arcane Spell, and Divine Spell labels), and the ability, gift, and no-prereq examples render as inline tier-and-price prose with a 'Disc:' shorthand and a 'Duration' field that do not exist in the book's actual card tables; two examples even alter real published cards. Third, class vocabulary is stale: 'fighter', 'warlock', and 'cleric' appear where the nine canonical class names belong [19-gm-guidance.qmd:71][19-gm-guidance.qmd:345]. Fourth, check notation breaks the Skill (Attribute) convention with a reversed attribute-skill pairing and two mixed attribute-skill option lists [19-gm-guidance.qmd:159][19-gm-guidance.qmd:214][19-gm-guidance.qmd:312]. Separately, the sample adventure's scenes are nested under unrelated general-advice headings (Scene 2 under Running Social Scenes, Scene 3 under The First Failure Matters, Scene 4 under Running This Fight), fracturing the fiction for a mid-chapter reader. What passes: every cross-reference resolves (social conflict, damage budget, combat, faction system, card templates anchors all exist), the em-dash law holds, the faction track's seven-point scale and per-action cap are coherent, and the adventure's milestone advance matches the advancement chapter; those strengths do not offset the blockers above.

evidence.claim: The group skill challenge is internally contradictory: the setup sentence stops the attempt at two failures, but the outcomes table lists a three-plus-failures row that can never trigger under that stop condition, so the chapter's own rules disagree and one outcome is unreachable.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The party needs 3 successes before 2 failures.

evidence.claim: The declared spell header template reads '(Spell)', yet every published spell card is labeled Cantrip, Arcane Spell, or Divine Spell, so a reader copying the template verbatim produces a label the book never uses; the chapter's own example contradicts its format line by using '(Arcane Spell)'.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: `### Name (Spell)` then a single field line

evidence.claim: The ability template and its examples present abilities as inline prose with the tier and price in parentheses plus a 'Disc:' shorthand, whereas real class abilities are five-column table rows with no price cell, since card prices live in the disciplines chapter's cost tables.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: **Shadow Strike (Adept, 4 DP).** Disc: 1 Stealth, 1 Sleight.

evidence.quote_or_excerpt: **Spark (Novice, 2 DP).** No prereq. Range: 30 ft. Duration: Instantaneous.

evidence.claim: Three passages use the pre-revision class nouns fighter, warlock, and cleric where the rulebook's nine canonical class names should appear, in the gold-spending example and in the adventure's next-hook suggestions.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Or the cleric's holy symbol. Or the fighter's family crest.

evidence.claim: Several checks break the book's check notation: one pairing is written attribute-first with the skill second, and two others list an attribute beside a skill as interchangeable options.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: make a Fortitude (Endurance) roll each day

evidence.claim: The sample adventure's scenes are misnested: Scene 2 through the Conclusion sit beneath general-advice headings that interrupt the fiction, so a reader following the section order is shuttled out of the adventure and into essays between scenes.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: ## Running Social Scenes

payload.argument: Refute: three mechanical layout defects block clean publication, though the chapter is structurally close. (1) This is the only chapter in the whole book that descends to fourth-level headings: the three example factions at 19-gm-guidance.qmd:451, 19-gm-guidance.qmd:463, and 19-gm-guidance.qmd:475 are marked '####', a depth no other chapter uses; the rendered PDF shows those headings receive none of the template's ornamental markers that levels one through three carry, so they land as bare text lines outside the book's heading design. Fix: replace them with bold run-in paragraph leads, the pattern every other chapter uses for sub-sub content. (2) The spell-card worked example at 19-gm-guidance.qmd:510 is the book's only heading nested inside a blockquote; it renders with a full ornamented heading while the other three card examples in the same template sections use bold name runs inside their quotes, giving four cards two distinct visual treatments. Fix: convert it to a bold run-in to match its siblings. (3) Range punctuation splits two ways within the chapter: en-dash spans at 19-gm-guidance.qmd:69 and 19-gm-guidance.qmd:111 versus a plain hyphen at 19-gm-guidance.qmd:191. Fix: harmonize. Everything else holds: zero em-dashes, '##' callout titles inside the '###' scenes stay out of the table of contents, heading levels never skip, cross-references resolve, and the tables are narrow enough to wrap without overflow.

evidence.claim: Fourth-level headings appear nowhere else in the book; in the rendered PDF the three faction headings show none of the ornamented markers the template applies to levels one through three, so they read as plain text lines.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: #### The Argent Circle

evidence.claim: The spell-card worked example is the book's single heading inside a blockquote; the other three template examples in the Spell Card and Ability Card sections use bold lead-in runs, so the four examples present as two different layouts.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: > ### Brimstone Burst (Arcane Spell)

evidence.claim: Within one chapter, numeric spans alternate between en-dash and hyphen punctuation for the same kind of range.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Expected play time: 3-4 hours.

evidence.claim: The callout titles embedded in the sample adventure's scenes are absorbed as callout titles and stay out of the table of contents, matching book convention; the chapter also contains zero em-dashes.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: ## For First-Time DAs

payload.argument: Refute. Framing: the chapter is four stacked functions, DA advice, a starter adventure, a faction subsystem, and the card-grammar reference. The frame holds; the defects are accuracy problems, not structural ones. Load-bearing: the Fortify Position faction action gives +5 temporary HP to a stronghold ([19:440]) while ch18's Fortify action gives +10 and explicitly stacks with the faction action ([18:137]); the adventure boss is Challenge 2 yet both of its attacks deal 6/9/12 ([19:304]), two tiers above the locked band for challenges 1-2, and its seal-breaking bonus is a flat damage add ([19:304]) where the book's phrasing is a damage-tier bump; the poultice heals 3 HP flat ([19:227]) though healing is budget-keyed. Convention violations that are also load-bearing under the standing list: class nouns outside the nine ([19:345], [19:71]), the generic +1 sword ([19:69]) against ch17's named-card rule, mixed skill-and-attribute checks ([19:214], [19:312]), a reversed attribute-first check ([19:159]), and flat check bonuses where the convention is a Boon ([19:251], [19:334]). Cosmetic: darkness modifiers differ within the chapter ([19:43] vs [19:163]), non-ladder vocabulary ([19:242] 'Harder', [19:53] 'Deadly'), a 1d3 die ([19:461]), 'surprise round' phrasing ([19:257]) that clashes with ch13's no-surprise-rounds rule, and the Brimstone Burst example diverges from the published card ([19:511]). Disposition buckets: mechanical, a safe micro-PR, covers every load-bearing item above except the three rulings below; substantive, a dispatched pass, covers converting the adventure loot into ch17-style item cards ([19:333-336]) and aligning the template examples with published cards; design-decision, Bruce's ruling with convention-anchored defaults, covers the encounter multiplier's mapping to ch20 bands ([19:53], default: keep and cross-reference), corruption accumulation past the threshold toward the unplayable cap ([19:175], default: keep, clarify that corruption continues past threshold), and Kelvath's damage ([19:304], default: band-compliant 2/4/6, or re-level the encounter if a deadlier boss is wanted). The chapter is shippable after a bounded, mostly mechanical fix pass; it is not shippable untouched.

payload.rationale: Topic t-01 (ch19 publishable as-is): 7 findings, all refute, zero support, quorum 4, reject_quorum 4 -> REJECTED. The chapter's four-function frame (DA advice, starter adventure, faction subsystem, card grammar) holds structurally: the author lens confirms voice consistency, the layout lens confirms zero em-dashes, clean cross-refs, and TOC-safe callouts, and the closing-balance audit's ch19 survivors (poultice, Kelvath band, Spark mismatch) are confirmed still present except Spark (already fixed). The refutes cluster on (1) the Kelvath stat block violating the locked monster bands plus a flat damage rider, (2) faction-action values drifting from ch18's canonical Fortify/Train, (3) the card-templates section misrepresenting the book's actual card grammar, (4) check-notation drift and stale class nouns, (5) small off-budget numbers (poultice 3, narration 2/3) and non-ladder modifiers (darkness -4, crafting ±1), (6) a self-contradictory skill-challenge threshold, and (7) the Brimstone Burst example teaching off-row center riders that also exist in the published ch11 card. No dissent. No rulings applied (no impasse, no judge).
payload.recommendation: REJECTED 7-0: ch19 is not publishable as-is; ship the disposition plan as ONE atomic ch19 PR plus a small ch11 cross-chapter fix. Load-bearing mechanical/canon fixes: (a) Kelvath (19:304) drops both primary attacks from 6/9/12 to 2/4/6 to conform to the locked C1-2 band (ch20: Bear C2 2/4/6); seal-break '+1 to all damage' becomes '+1 damage tier' (the Overchannel convention, matching Water Bolt's own 19:314 language); (b) faction actions reconcile to ch18: Fortify Position (19:440) +5 temp HP -> +10 temp HP with a @sec-strongholds cross-ref (ch18:137 Fortify grants +10 and stacks with this faction action), Train (19:438) +1 -> +2 (ch18:146 Train grants +2 and replaces the faction Train); (c) poultice (19:227) heals 3 HP -> 4 HP (Novice Standard row; healing is budget-keyed); (d) first-combat narration (19:289) '2 damage'/'3 damage' made DR-consistent by adding 'after its armor' (Brawn +2 Basic Melee 3/4 minus DR 1 = 2/3); (e) skill-challenge intro (19:230) '3 successes before 2 failures' reconciled with the 2-failure and 3+-failure outcome rows; (f) card-templates section (19:493-540) aligned to the real book grammar: spell label '(Spell)' -> the published Cantrip/Arcane Spell/Divine Spell labels, ability example converted from inline prose to the ch05 five-column table row (Shadow Strike verbatim), no-prereq example converted to the published Spark (Cantrip) card, gift example converted to the ch04 table-row format, W:/S:/St: unified to Weak:/Standard:/Strong:; (g) the Brimstone Burst example becomes the published card, which requires the same PR to strip the off-row center +2/+3 riders from the published ch11 card (9+2=11, 12+3=15 are not rows; compliant Fireball pattern is 9+3=12); (h) check notation: 19:159 Fortitude (Endurance) -> Endurance (Fortitude), 19:214 'Knowledge or Persuasion' -> 'Arcana or Persuasion', 19:292 'Knowledge or Reason' -> 'Arcana or Insight', 19:312 'Arcana or Reason' -> 'Arcana or Insight'; (i) stale class nouns: 19:345 warlock/cleric/fighter -> Arcanist/Shepherd/Protector, 19:71 'the fighter's armor' -> 'the Protector's armor'; (j) 'A +1 sword at level 2 is a big deal' (19:69) -> 'a single enchanted sword' (ch17 bans generic +1 items); (k) 'surprise round' (19:257) -> ch13's ambush phrasing (ambushing side acts first, Surprised -2 on first roll); (l) darkness -4 (19:163) -> -2 (harmonizes with 19:43 and ch06's Hard ladder); (m) 'Standard (Harder, -2)' (19:242) -> 'Hard (-2)'; (n) faction perk vocabulary: 'Allied Boon' and 'unique faction boons' (19:371/415/420/461/474) -> 'Allied Favor'/'unique faction favors' to avoid colliding with the Boon mechanic keyword; (o) reputation-track table (19:368-371) gains the Allied 50% discount so the summary and the benefits section (19:401-428) do not drift; (p) #### faction headings (19:451/463/475, the book's only level-4 headings, render unornamented) -> bold run-in leads; (q) the blockquote heading '> ### Brimstone Burst (Arcane Spell)' (19:510) -> bold run-in to match the sibling examples; (r) '3-4 hours' (19:191) -> en-dash to harmonize with 19:69/19:111. Design-flavored defaults implemented and flagged veto-revertible: encounter-multiplier section (19:49-64) gains one sentence tying ×N to Challenge bands and a party-size step (six or more heroes one step harder, three or fewer one step easier); Kelvath's tether (19:304) tightened from 20 ft to 10 ft so the tactical note is honest in the 40-ft chamber, and the false claim that Water Bolt 'outranges most spells and bows' (19:310) reworded (bows are 80/320); crafting table (19:141-145) converts ±1 odd modifiers to Bane on Weak / Boon on Strong. Kept as-is with notes: the 1d3 delivery roll (19:461) matches ch18's Recruit 1d3 precedent; the interleaved callouts inside the sample adventure render as sidebars out of the TOC per book convention and stay. All items are mechanical or canon-determined except the five flagged defaults; none is blocked.
